summary: Outcome per dollar is the frontier. We’re advancing it at every layer: FLOPs-efficient pretraining (MAI Base 2 - https://lnkd.in/gs9RC95k), long RL climbs (Rocket - https://lnkd.in/gyEbHeUZ), and token-efficient models (7 new MAI models announced last week - https://lnkd.in/gnE_72nm). All driving better economics for our customers. By building models and products together, we can keep hill-climbing and building models that deliver real-world tasks and passing the gains directly to customers, while staying open to every frontier model. | 303 comments on LinkedIn
body_markdown: ✈️ 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗥𝗟 𝗱𝗶𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲 Satya, read the MAI architecture with an aviation eye, and it is an airline operations system: 🛫 Controller = Operations Control Centre 🧑✈️ Rollout workers = flights in the air 📡 Sampler = dispatch 🛠️ Recovery checkpoints = MRO 🗼 Runtime management = ATC ━━━━━━━━━━━━ Here is the idea aviation can lend you. Twin-engine jets cross oceans only because of ETOPS: every point on the route must stay within reach of a diversion airport. An RL run that lasts weeks is a long-haul flight. Checkpoints are not storage; they are diversion airfields. Place them by risk, not by the clock. Aviation never won on speed. It won on dispatch reliability. Outcome per dollar is the fare. Outcome per run that lands safely is the airline. 🛬 Regds Prof. Dr Sanjay Kumar, h.c.
